headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, networked execution can conflict with caveman’s MCP/file workflows, creating default-path data leakage and cascading errors unless tightly isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute tool calls; caveman uses MCP and touches CLAUDE.md, project notes, and memory files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGen consumes caveman-authored files or MCP outputs as trusted text. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF AutoGen ingests caveman-written files or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or notes directory
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic instruction loading from CLAUDE.md and notes
Add provenance tags to MCP/file outputs
Review any file-derived prompts before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while caveman stores session logs, memory files, and project notes. If they share a workspace, sensitive application data can move from caveman files into AutoGen’s networked context and out to model providers. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or project directory
IF AutoGen is configured to send file contents to external model providers
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts
Exclude memory/session files from AutoGen inputs
Redact secrets before handoff
Restrict AutoGen egress to approved endpoints only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; caveman uses MCP and file-based project artifacts. Even though caveman has no network egress and no explicit write capability is listed, overlapping access to shared files can still cause race conditions or clobbered notes. Uncertainty about caveman’s write behavior pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF caveman’s MCP-backed tools mutate files while AutoGen is running
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Turn off concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Snapshot files before each agent writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code or structured outputs that caveman may ingest through files or MCP-backed workflows. caveman’s content-writing role suggests it may render or reuse upstream text, so an error in AutoGen can propagate into downstream artifacts without verification. The profiles do not prove blind trust, but the pathway exists and is not mitigated by default.
conditions: IF caveman consumes AutoGen-produced text as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require a review step before caveman uses AutoGen output
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted by default
Add schema validation for exchanged artifacts
Limit AutoGen to draft-only outputs

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad egress, while caveman stores session logs and memory files. That can create a modest compliance mismatch if regulated or sensitive data is placed into shared notes, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification conflict. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data.
conditions: IF regulated data is written into caveman memory/session files
IF AutoGen forwards that data to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared notes
Add a data-classification checklist
Use a DPA-approved provider only
Purge logs after each session
